tool.name: LEMUR
tool.command: Rscript '$__tool_directory__/lemur.R' --input_rds '$sce' --meta_table '$meta_table' --cell_id_column '$cell_id_column' --condition_column '$condition_column' #if str($batch_column): --batch_column '$batch_column' #end if --contrast_condition '$contrast_condition' --reference_condition '$reference_condition' --n_embedding '$n_embedding' --test_fraction '$test_fraction' --output_umap 'umap.$plot_format' --output_volcano 'volcano.$plot_format' --output_de 'de_results.tsv' #if str($sel_gene): --sel_gene '$sel_gene' --output_gene_umap 'gene_umap.$plot_format' --output_gene_hist 'gene_hist.$plot_format' #end if --use_harmony '$use_harmony' --plot_format '$plot_format' --plot_width '$plot_width' --plot_height '$plot_height' --run_tumor_analysis '$tumor_analysis_cond.run_tumor_analysis' #if str($tumor_analysis_cond.run_tumor_analysis) == 'yes': --output_chr_scatter 'chr_scatter.$plot_format' --output_tumor_umap 'tumor_umap.$plot_format' --output_tumor_neigh 'tumor_neigh.tsv' --tumor_annotation_column '$tumor_analysis_cond.tumor_annotation_column' --chrom1_name '$tumor_analysis_cond.chrom1_name' --chrom2_name '$tumor_analysis_cond.chrom2_name' --chrom1_thresh '$tumor_analysis_cond.chrom1_thresh' --chrom2_thresh '$tumor_analysis_cond.chrom2_thresh' #end if

param.name: meta_table
param.label: Sample metadata table (TSV)
param.help: TSV file with one row per sample/cell. Must contain columns for condition and optionally for batch.

param.name: cell_id_column
param.label: Cell ID column
param.help: Column in metadata that contains the cell IDs matching colnames of SCE

param.name: condition_column
param.label: Condition column
param.help: Select the condition column (e.g., treatment vs control). Only appears after loading metadata.

param.name: batch_column
param.label: Batch column (optional)
param.help: Optional batch variable (e.g., patient ID). Only appears after loading metadata.

param.name: test_fraction
param.label: Fraction of genes used for training

param.name: run_tumor_analysis
param.label: Run tumor-specific classification (chromosome-based)
param.help: Optional: classifies cells as tumor/non-tumor based on chromosome gain/loss (as in the glioblastoma example). Not applicable to all datasets — enable only if relevant to your data.

param.name: tumor_annotation_column
param.label: Tumor annotation column in rowData
param.help: Used for tumor classification. Default is 'chromosome'. Override if your SCE uses a different annotation column.

param.name: chrom1_name
param.label: Chromosome expected to be gained in tumor cells
param.help: Name/ID of the chromosome expected to show increased expression ('gain') in tumor cells, as it appears in the tumor annotation column above. This whole-chromosome gain/loss classification is specific to cancer types with known chromosome-arm-level copy number alterations (e.g. glioblastoma, default: chromosome 7 gain) — confirm this pattern applies to your cancer type/dataset before using it.

param.name: chrom2_name
param.label: Chromosome expected to be lost in tumor cells
param.help: Name/ID of the chromosome expected to show decreased expression ('loss') in tumor cells, as it appears in the tumor annotation column above (default: chromosome 10, matching the glioblastoma example of chromosome 10 loss). As with the gained chromosome, confirm this pattern applies to your cancer type/dataset.

param.name: chrom1_thresh
param.label: Minimum expression threshold for the gained chromosome
param.help: Minimum mean expression of the gained chromosome (above) required to classify a cell as tumor.

param.name: chrom2_thresh
param.label: Maximum expression threshold for the lost chromosome
param.help: Maximum mean expression of the lost chromosome (above) required to classify a cell as tumor.

tool.help:
LEMUR identifies transcriptional differences across conditions in latent space using single-cell RNA-seq data. This tool wraps the core LEMUR workflow (latent embedding multivariate regression) and can be applied to single-cell data from any tissue or cell type — it is not limited to any specific disease or dataset.
**Inputs:** - A `SingleCellExperiment` object in RDS format. - Design formula indicating batch and condition variables. - Parameters for dimensionality and model training. - Optionally, a gene ID for extra gene-specific plots. - Apply Harmony alignment: If selected, the latent space is aligned using Harmony before differential expression analysis. - Selectable output format for all plots: PDF, PNG, or JPG.
**Why use `SingleCellExperiment` (SCE)?** LEMUR uses the `SingleCellExperiment` (SCE) format because it is the standard Bioconductor structure for single-cell data in R. Unlike Seurat or AnnData, SCE is lightweight, interoperable, and not tied to a specific framework. It cleanly separates assays (e.g., expression values), cell metadata (`colData`), feature metadata (`rowData`), and reduced dimensions (`reducedDims`).
For LEMUR to work correctly, the SCE object **must include**: - **`counts()`**: matrix of raw (non-normalized) integer counts, required for the pseudobulk differential expression testing performed by `find_de_neighborhoods()`. - **`logcounts()`**: matrix of log-normalized gene expression, used for model fitting and visualization. - **`colData`**: must contain the variables referenced in the `design` formula (e.g., `patient_id`, `condition`).
You can easily convert Seurat objects using `as.SingleCellExperiment()` in R.
**Outputs:** - UMAP plot - Volcano plot - Table of differentially expressed neighborhoods (without neighborhood list-column) - Gene UMAP + histogram plots if a gene ID is given
**Optional tumor-specific classification:** Enabling "Run tumor-specific classification" performs a chromosome gain/loss-based tumor/non-tumor cell classification, using two configurable chromosome-arm markers (default: chromosome 7 gain / chromosome 10 loss, as used in the glioblastoma example below). This approach can be applied to other tumor types with known chromosome-level copy number alterations by adjusting the chromosome names and thresholds to match your data — it is disabled by default since it's only relevant if your dataset includes this kind of copy-number-based tumor signal. When enabled, it adds three outputs: a chromosome expression scatter plot, a tumor/non-tumor UMAP plot, and a table of differentially expressed neighborhoods restricted to the classified tumor cells.
This analysis was inspired by the glioblastoma example in the official LEMUR repository, which also has more details on the core method: https://github.com/const-ae/lemur
